newsitem.title: UK: Italy to start new oil-fired Brindisi power station.
newsitem.headline: Italy to start new oil-fired Brindisi power station.

text.p: A new 2,500 megawatt power station in Brindisi, Italy burning low sulphur fuel oil is due to start operation in the first 10 days of December, sources within Italian state power utility Enel said on Monday.
The station, Brindisi Sud, consists of four units of 600 MW each, and two of these are expected to start up gradually while flue gas desulphurisation (FGD) equipment is fitted to the other units.

A company executive said each unit would burn about 800,000 tonnes of fuel oil per year and would have to use 0.25 percent sulphur fuel oil to comply with European law, which stipulates maximum sulphur emissions of 400 milligrams per cubic metre.

Desulphurisation equipment is due to be fitted to the four trains in February, May, September and November 1997, he said. Coal infrastructure was also being constructed at the site, and coal burning could begin in 1998.

Traders in international oil markets said the start-up of the plant was a bullish factor as winter approaches. They said Enel bought two large cargoes of Congolese and Nigerian low sulphur fuel oil last week to feed the new plant.
